page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 2 physical AMD EPYC 9T24 cores running at 2.7 GHz with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB per core, and does not include local storage or integrated GPUs. Network connectivity is delivered via a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring 3075.37 and Geekbench text processing scoring 2483.0, both placing in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and Passmark CPU encryption tests fall within the average range. However, the instance exhibits weaknesses in memory read bandwidth, with cached small-block reads at 303.96 GB/sec and uncached large-block reads at 36.57 GB/sec. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, software compilation with Clang, and ray tracing benchmarks also rank in the bottom 25%.

The absence of bundled local storage requires reliance on external block storage, which may impact I/O-intensive operations. This is reflected in the weak database operations and Redis SET performance benchmarks. Qualitatively, the dedicated CPU allocation offers consistent compute performance for CPU-bound tasks, making it a cost-efficient option for workloads that do not require high memory density or local NVMe storage. Appropriate workloads include single-threaded processing, text processing, and lightweight compute tasks, while it is less suitable for memory-intensive databases or high-throughput web serving.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor running at 2.7 GHz, paired with 8.0 GB of RAM. Operating on the KVM hypervisor, this x86_64 instance lacks local storage and integrated GPUs, relying on a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark data shows strong single-core CPU and text processing capabilities, though multi-threaded decompression and memory read bandwidth are relatively weak. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes this instance a qualitatively cost-efficient option for dedicated CPU tasks that do not require high memory capacity. It is best suited for text processing, single-threaded applications, and lightweight compute workloads, while database operations and high-throughput web serving are limited by its memory and storage constraints.
